cause_quote: The iOS node services were added parsing params with a default formatter: `let formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter()` / `guard let start = formatter.date(from: params.startISO)`, which rejects fractional seconds.
user_saw: On iOS nodes, calendar.add and reminders.add failed with CALENDAR_INVALID/REMINDERS_INVALID for timestamps like 2026-11-08T10:00:00.000Z, and calendar/motion queries silently used their default date range.
summary: Added a shared OpenClawISO8601.date(from:) parser that accepts fractional seconds and used it in the iOS calendar, reminders and motion services.
reasoning: The removed default-options ISO8601DateFormatter parsing is older than the graft; full-history listing shows the services landed on main in #11756 (6aedc54, after an earlier revert), and its diff (via gh api) contains the same `ISO8601DateFormatter()` + `formatter.date(from:)` parsing in Calendar, Motion and Reminders services. Later commits were refactors that kept this parsing, so the fractional-seconds rejection shipped with the feature.
